cohort: Women diagnosed with uterine rupture and admitted to the emergency unit between January 2016 and December 2017 at a tertiary care hospital
finding: The incidence of uterine rupture was 32/10,000 deliveries, and rupture of an unscarred uterus was associated with higher maternal and fetal mortality.
mod_finding: The study examined uterine rupture in the context of both scarred and unscarred uteruses, finding that while rupture of a scarred uterus was more common (likely due to the rising rate of cesarean sections), rupture of an unscarred uterus was associated with greater maternal and fetal mortality.
